benchmark:
Measured on the dev machine (AMD Ryzen 5 7530U, Node v24.13.1, runner 'dev', seed 42, batch 1,000, about 2,400–3,600 samples per point). Load average was about 5 because other agents were running at the same time. Re-run on the lab machine before the final defence.

Representative run, mean / p50 / p95 in ns per op:
- add: 10^3 79.0 / 70.5 / 113.5; 10^4 87.5 / 78.1 / 120.5; 10^5 84.3 / 79.7 / 113.3. Ratio 1.07.
- mayContain (50% members): 10^3 71.0 / 68.2 / 91.4; 10^4 75.9 / 74.0 / 91.8; 10^5 85.3 / 80.3 / 128.8. Ratio 1.20.

Across 3 runs, the add ratio was 1.07–1.35 and the mayContain ratio 0.86–1.44 (limit 2). Every mean was 70–102 ns (target 200 ns or less). The curve is flat, as O(k) = O(1) predicts; the small rise from 10^3 to 10^5 comes from cache (the bit array grows from 1.25 KB to 125 KB).

Memory (bytes per key):
- Allocated: 1.252 at 10^3, 1.250 at 10^4 and 1.250 at 10^5.
- Measured with --expose-gc: 13.3, 1.78 and 1.257. At 10^3 the fixed object overhead of about 12 KB dominates.

Measured false-positive rate at nDesign = 16,384: 0.907% with 10^5 probes and 0.845% with 10^6 (expected 0.819%). At 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5 keys it was 0.79–0.85%. Bit fill was 0.504, against 0.503 in theory.

Replacing `%` with an exact floor-division modulo (modU32) cut add by about 25% (roughly 80 ns down to 60 ns in a tight loop). Its exactness is proven in comments and a 5·10^6-value check against `%` found no mismatch.
